title: Kokoro backend discarded all but the first generated audio segment
description:
Both KokoroBackend._generate_mlx and ._generate_torch call generators that
yield one result per *segment* -- Kokoro's pipeline splits long text into
speakable chunks internally due to a model sequence-length limit (not by
paragraph). Both backends took only the first yielded result
(next(iter(gen)) / results[0]), silently discarding every subsequent
segment. Any text needing more than one segment was truncated to just its
first chunk, with no error, no warning -- the job completed normally and
reported 'done'.

Reproduced live via Pilobol.us: a ~9400-character article produced a 26-
second clip (the first paragraph) before the fix, 549 seconds (the full
article) after. Short inputs were unaffected, single segment either way --
this is why Auritus's own demo clips, all short, never surfaced it.

Fixed: cli/src/auritus/tts/kokoro.py, commit b294650 -- concatenate every
yielded segment's audio before building the WAV.

The already-published broken audio for one already-'done' job
(Pilobol.us's own first real article) had to be manually regenerated with
the fixed backend and its S3 object overwritten directly, since the job API
has no way to reset a 'done' job back to pending/claimable for
reprocessing -- a gap worth its own ticket if this happens again at any
scale (right now it's a one-off manual fix, not a real backlog).
